svg.title: Classical Time Series vs Deep Learning
svg.desc: Classical models state their assumptions, so they hold up in small samples and yield interpretation; deep learning relaxes assumptions but demands data and careful validation design.
svg.text: Classical Time Series vs Deep Learning
Does a person design the structure, or does the data learn the representation
A handful to a few dozen
Estimable from a few hundred points
Read directly from coefficients and IRFs
Needs long series or many of them
it must be designed in separately
Holds up even on short samples
On short series, a structural assumption is information
It pulls ahead as data accumulates
Before the crossover it struggles to beat the classical model
What each component means is fixed in advance
The representation is learned from the input window
What the layers built is explained only after the fact
Classical models state their assumptions, holding up in small samples and yielding interpretation.
Deep learning relaxes assumptions but demands data and careful validation design.
Leave what structure explains to the model
and pass only the residual to the network
Next (17): sequential processing vs convolution and attention — RNN / LSTM vs TCN / Transformer.
